title: Introduce synthetic workload generator and changelog prioritizer
author: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: Adds a lightweight synthetic workload generator (synth-prober) to create deterministic, seedable usage traces for newly onboarded models and a changelog prioritizer job that scores metadata deltas by estimated customer impact and telemetry signal. Context: Model churn and frequent minor metadata edits produced very noisy release notes and made rollout triage slow. The synth-prober generates representative traffic shapes (short-chat, long-context, high-embedding-rate) so the registry can compute stable perf fingerprints and prioritize changelog entries that correlate with measurable quality or cost impact. Implementation: 1) synth/runner: new package that generates synthetic requests from configurable templates and emits CSV/JSON traces; 2) metadata/impact_score: introduce an "impact_score" field for model versions computed from delta heuristics + optional telemetry crosswalk; 3) release/prioritizer: scheduled job that ranks changelog fragments and prunes low-impact noise while preserving compliance-relevant changes; 4) onboarding pipeline hook: runs synth-prober on model upload in a sandboxed job and attaches perf signatures to model profile; 5) UI/notes: compact changelog preview with top-3 prioritized bullets and link to full delta. Backward compatibility: opt-in via a new registry flag (modelRegistry.enableSynthProber=false by default) so existing flows are unchanged. Security: sandbox execution, sanitized sample inputs, and KMS-scoped storage for probe artifacts. Testing & metrics: includes unit tests for scoring heuristics, a small integration test that runs synth-prober against a dummy quantized model, and added KG metrics: synth_runs_total, prioritized_changelog_count, and impact_score_histogram. Migration: a migration job annotates recent 30 days of model versions with a computed impact_score (best-effort). Rollout plan: gated canary (10% of onboard flows enabled) for two weeks with telemetry watch. Checklist: - [x] design doc (linked in ENG-1984) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs updated (onboarding + release notes UX) - [x] Linear link: ENG-1984 - [x] telemetry dashboards added - [x] migration job included Commits: see commits field below. Changed areas: listed in changed_files. Motivation & tradeoffs: We avoid aggressive auto-pruning; the prioritizer exposes a confidence level and keeps a trace of suppressed items to allow audit and rehydrate release notes if needed. We opted for a seedable synthetic generator rather than running real traffic replay for privacy and reproducibility. Additional notes: the impact_score algorithm is intentionally pluggable (we ship a baseline heuristics impl; future work includes a small ranking model trained on historical regressions).

review_comments: Samir: Can we make the default schedule configurable from console? -- Reply: Yes, added a config key and documented it.
Elena: Impact score math needs a tie-breaker when telemetry is missing. -- Reply: Added a deterministic fallback that favors latency regressions > cost increases.
Jonah: Sandbox resource limits look high for canary. Please reduce and add circuit-breaker. -- Reply: Lowered CPU/memory, added circuit-breaker and a fail-open flag for emergencies.
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (flaky on first run, re-run fixed)
release_notes: Adds an opt-in synthetic workload generator to compute stable perf signatures during model onboarding and a changelog prioritizer that surfaces high-impact metadata changes in release notes; configurable, audited, and initially gated for canary rollout.
